recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-16986 unless a future work-group issue reopens open-ended Timing ranges or changes the paired Max-element semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-16986 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core datatypes request to clarify Timing.repeat count/countMax, duration/durationMax, frequency/frequencyMax, and period/periodMax by making the base element the lower bound when its Max partner is present and making the Max element wording follow the frequencyMax range pattern.
initial_application: The issue was applied by SVN revision 14076, represented in git as 3c90bd518312a0c35842ca968584ee9d017dba8c with subject '16986 - clarification on Timing definitions'. That commit changed source/datatypes/timing.xml definitions for count, countMax, duration, durationMax, frequency, and period to add the requested lower-bound/range language; Jira's application comment cites the same SVN revision.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists Timing as an active datatype and marks it normative, so source/datatypes/timing.xml is current build scope. The current spreadsheet still contains the lower-bound language for count, duration, frequency, and period and paired range language for the Max elements. Existing Timing.repeat invariants require countMax, durationMax, and periodMax to have their corresponding base element. A 2017 Zulip thread confirms implementer confusion around count/countMax ranges but does not conflict with the applied resolution; Confluence searches found no contrary work-group record.
reconciliation: No source edit was made. The authoritative Timing spreadsheet already conveys the requested range semantics, and further prose changes would be redundant rather than necessary for current implementer understanding.
